clue.text: Last to be dismissed, first catch

indicators.note: first says the catch word goes at the front, ahead of the dismissal

parts.note: to catch something is to grip or hold it
a batsman who is dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: the final batsman is sent back, caught on the first ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The (4,3) count shows this is the phrasal verb, not the noun 'holdout'. 'Last' looks like part of a cricket phrase but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to endure or keep going, which is the sense of the phrasal verb meaning resist giving way.

clue.text: Cut a couple of journalists

parts.note: the phrase signals two separate members of the press, the first a hack, a hired writer
the second of the pair is an ED, short for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper laying off two of its reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of journalists' supplies two press people: HACK (a jobbing writer) and ED (an editor).
explanation.definitionFit: Hacked is a past tense verb for chopped roughly, a synonym of cut.

clue.text: Transparent top worn by Puck?

indicators.note: a hat worn by someone sits around them, so the top goes around the sprite

parts.note: a lid is the top of a container
Puck is the mischievous sprite of A Midsummer Night's Dream, an imp

explanation.surface: A see-through costume top for an actor playing Puck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' sounds like clothing given the 'worn' picture, but it is a lid, the top of a jar.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid describes water or prose that is perfectly clear, a synonym of transparent.

clue.text: Respect one formulating a "known unknown"

indicators.note: formulating means putting together afresh, so the letters of the two words are reworked

explanation.surface: Rumsfeld-style jargon: respecting someone who coins the phrase 'known unknown'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formulating' rearranges RESPECT ONE into the (4,6) phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supposedly hidden that everybody is aware of is a paradox neatly captured by the playful phrase.

clue.text: Regret a serviceman carries shocking weaponry

indicators.note: the phrase carries the letters within it, spanning the end of one word and the start of the next two

explanation.surface: Lamenting that a soldier is armed with an electric stun gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' picks the letters from regreT A SERviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: A stun gun that fires electrified darts literally delivers shocks, so it is weaponry that shocks.

clue.text: An extra drink? Cheers!

parts.note: a perk is an extra benefit on top of pay
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone offered another drink responds with a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers!' looks like a toast but is the verb: becomes more cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers, as a verb, means brightens or becomes happier, which the phrasal verb also means.

clue.text: I reopened building having laid the foundations

indicators.note: building puts something together, so the letters of the words are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A developer boasts of reopening a site after starting the construction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges I REOPENED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be first to develop something is to establish the groundwork that others follow.

clue.text: Dare to feel up and down, but not at first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the search word is dropped

parts.note: to frisk is to search someone by patting them up and down

explanation.surface: A cheeky challenge to grope someone, phrased as a dare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not at first' removes the F from FRISK.
explanation.definitionFit: To dare something is to chance or hazard it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Well in ground provides source of energy

indicators.note: in places the word for healthy inside the earth word

parts.note: ground is earth or soil
well in the sense of healthy is hale

explanation.surface: A well sunk into the ground yields fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like an oil well but means healthy (HALE), set 'in' SOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Petroleum extracted from sedimentary rock is a fossil fuel, a source of power.

clue.text: Ratty and Mole holding up a pick-up truck

indicators.note: holding means the spy word surrounds the vehicle

parts.note: a mole or spy is a plant

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the vehicle word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a ute is an Australian utility vehicle, a pick-up

explanation.surface: Wind in the Willows characters Ratty and Mole holding up a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ratty' is not the Wind in the Willows water rat but the adjective, and 'Mole' is a spy, not his friend. 'up' turns the truck word round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is informal British for irritable, which is what sulky and bad-tempered means.

clue.text: Moving in/out of team up the valley

indicators.note: moving a word out of another removes it
out of says the small word leaves the longer one

parts.note: to team up is to combine

explanation.surface: Someone moving in and out of a team based up a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving in out of' takes IN out of COMBINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A combe is a short steep valley, a word common in southern English place names.

clue.text: Fitful rest before dawn

indicators.note: before puts the pause word ahead

parts.note: to stop is to rest or pause
the dawn of something is its start

explanation.surface: Restless sleep in the hours before daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitful describes something irregular and intermittent, going in bursts and pauses.

clue.text: English woman meets House representatives

indicators.note: meets places the two parts side by side

parts.note: a miss is a young woman
Aries is the first house of the zodiac in astrology

explanation.surface: An Englishwoman meets members of the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' suggests Parliament, but it is an astrological house, ARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Emissaries are envoys sent on a mission, people who act for someone else.

clue.text: Food and drink left for daughter

indicators.note: left for daughter means one letter replaces the other

parts.note: mead is a drink made from honey
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Supper and a drink left out for a daughter coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the D of MEAD for L.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal is an occasion of eating, and by extension the food served.

clue.text: Fever results when small boy touches a girl

indicators.note: touches says the parts meet side by side

parts.note: Carl is a boy's name
Tina is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A child falls ill after a boy touches a girl at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlatina is another name for scarlet fever, an infection with a red rash.

clue.text: Sign of Labour/Tory grip

parts.note: a Tory is a Conservative, abbreviated Con
traction is grip, as of tyres on a road

explanation.surface: Political commentary on how the parties hold power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party, but is childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightening of the womb is a sign that childbirth has begun.

clue.text: Wordsmith finds account is entered in rewritten note

indicators.note: entered in places the account and the small word inside the shuffled letters
rewritten means the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: a log is a record or account

explanation.surface: A writer finds a bank account mentioned in an edited memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' shuffles the letters of 'note' into NEOT, which then holds the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A coiner of new words is a craftsman of language, which wordsmith suggests.

clue.text: Chorister arranged to miss first song at oratory

indicators.note: arranged as in music: the remaining letters are set out in a new order
to miss means the chosen letter is left out of the singer
first takes the opening letter of the word song

explanation.surface: A choirboy's arrangement skips the first hymn at a chapel service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to miss' drops S from CHORISTER, leaving CHORITER, which 'arranged' rearranges. 'oratory' looks like a chapel but means public speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive public speaking, which oratory also names.

clue.text: Influence catch — switch positions

parts.note: the rub is a catch or snag, as in Hamlet's there's the rub
a switch is either off or on

explanation.surface: Fumbling with a catch and swapping places.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a habit or quality on to someone is to influence them.

clue.text: Resident champion follows the crowd

indicators.note: follows puts the champion after the crowd

parts.note: the house is the audience in a theatre
a champion is a title holder

explanation.surface: A local champion who goes along with the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who occupies a dwelling as owner or tenant lives there.

clue.text: Regretted it being in black and white

indicators.note: being in places the small word within the colour word

parts.note: pied means patched in two colours, typically black and white, as a magpie

explanation.surface: Remorse over something being printed in black and white.
explanation.definitionFit: To have pitied someone is to have felt sorry for them, a sense close to regret.

clue.text: Looking up word for "layer": a hen, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down entry, looking up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lamina is a thin layer or plate

explanation.surface: Looking up a dictionary word for 'layer', a laying hen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' looks like a laying hen but means a thin sheet; the definition is the hen.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen is an example of a creature, so the 'perhaps' flags a definition by example.

clue.text: Sound horn travelling to and fro

indicators.note: travelling to and fro says the word goes the same in each direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A driver honking while driving back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same both ways, and is also TO followed by OT, 'to' turned to 'fro'.
explanation.definitionFit: To toot is to blow a short blast on a car horn.

clue.text: Moving in and out of base

indicators.note: moving the letters around shuffles them into a new order

explanation.surface: Soldiers moving in and out of their base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges IN AND OUT OF, ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundation is the underlying support of a building, its bottom layer.

clue.text: 20th-century wordsmith was indecisive

definitions.meaning: Alfred ... was an English poet, author of The Highwayman
said no then yes, dithering between the two

explanation.definitionFit: The poet Alfred is a twentieth-century writer, and dithering between negative and affirmative is indecision.

clue.text: Open with key finally, moving to front

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the island word
moving to front shifts that letter to the start

parts.note: a key is a low island or reef, as in the Florida Keys

explanation.surface: Unlocking a door with a key, then moving to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is a low island, REEF; 'finally, moving to front' brings its last letter F to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Open and free both describe something available or unrestricted.

clue.text: Further strengthen defence on right — Everton's front two score, if included

indicators.note: on says the rest follows the abbreviation
front picks the first letter of the football club
included puts the small word inside the number

parts.note: a score is twenty, so two score is forty

explanation.surface: Football punditry: shore up the right side of the back line, as Everton's strikers might score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defence' reads as part of the football picture but ends the definition, and 'front two' is a red herring: 'front' alone is the indicator. Everton is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster the defensive works of a place again is to strengthen it once more.

clue.text: Southern France backs introduction of old patois

indicators.note: introduction means putting something in, so the letter goes inside
backs means the region word is read in reverse

parts.note: the Midi is the south of France

explanation.surface: The south of France supports bringing back an old dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' reverses MIDI to IDIM, and 'introduction of' places O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a dialect or form of speech peculiar to a people, which patois also names.

clue.text: Sisters' building firm closing, then opening

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: closing takes the last letter of the word then

parts.note: a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: A building firm shutting down, then starting up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sisters' building' looks like a construction firm run by sisters, but means nuns' house.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent is a community house where nuns live, nuns being sisters.

clue.text: Check pulse after shocking incident

parts.note: to scan is to check over
dal is a pulse, a dish of lentils or split peas

explanation.surface: A medic taking a patient's pulse after a traumatic event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' is not a heartbeat but the legume, DAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is an outrageous event causing public shock.
